one_line: Mostly clean day; one unsupported Databricks take and a few minor wording issues.

findings.quote: Agent-scale query bills no longer have to be budgeted at warehouse rates that scale linearly with query volume.
findings.instruction: Rewrite the take so it reports Databricks' claim as a claim (e.g. 'Databricks says its engine decouples agent query volume from bill growth') rather than asserting that budgeting has changed. The source says only that the engine is architected to serve more queries on the same resources.
Drop the claim that the older Flash is retired, or soften it to 'replaced'. The body says only that Gemini 4 Hydrogen succeeds 3.8 Flash, which does not establish retirement.

dropped_findings.quote: and banks are scrambling to respond
dropped_findings.instruction: Check the headline claim 'banks are scrambling to respond' against the WSJ source. If the source does not say this, replace it with wording the source supports. This is a characterisation attributed to banks as a group.

note: verdict rule: major >= 1 (A reader would notice this. Ratifiable with notes, and worth a look before it ships.) | 1 finding(s) dropped: quote not found verbatim in the target text, or criterion inapplicable to this issue
